label: Attention Is All You Need
description: Vaswani et al. (2017) introduced the transformer architecture, replacing recurrence and convolution with multi-head self-attention. The foundational paper for modern foundation models.
abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
key_findings: Multi-head self-attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
Dispensing with recurrence enables massive parallelization during training, drastically reducing compute time.
Positional encodings provide sequence order without recurrence.
significance: Foundational architecture for modern LLMs, multimodal models, and agent backbones.

label: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3)
description: Brown et al. (2020) demonstrated that scaling language models to 175B parameters enables few-shot in-context learning without task-specific fine-tuning.
abstract: We train GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, and test its few-shot performance across NLP tasks. GPT-3 achieves strong performance on many benchmarks, often matching or exceeding the performance of fine-tuned models.
key_findings: In-context learning capability emerges as parameter count scales to 175B.
Few-shot prompting outperforms zero-shot prompting across semantic and reasoning benchmarks.
Generalization occurs without gradient updates during inference.
significance: Established the modern paradigm of general-purpose foundation models driven by prompt context.

label: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
description: Park et al. (2023) introduced the computational architecture for generative agents combining memory stream, reflection trees, and retrieval scoring.
abstract: We introduce generative agents—computational software agents that simulate believable human behavior. Generative agents draw on an architecture that extends a large language model to store a complete record of the agent's experiences using natural language, synthesize those memories over time into higher-level reflections, and retrieve them dynamically to plan behavior.
key_findings: Memory Stream: Comprehensive chronological record of raw observations.
Retrieval Score = Recency × Importance × Relevance, optimizing context injection.
Reflection Tree: Periodic higher-order synthesis questions that generate abstract insights from raw records.
significance: Direct architectural parent of Starlight Dreaming Engine and the Reflection Substrate in second-brain-vault.

label: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
description: Shinn et al. (2023) demonstrated that language agents can learn from trial and error by generating verbal self-reflections and maintaining an episodic memory of errors.
abstract: We present Reflexion, an approach that endows an agent with dynamic memory and self-reflection capabilities for reasoning, decision-making, and programming tasks. Reflexion agents verbally reflect on task feedback signals, then maintain their own reflective text in an episodic memory buffer to induce better decision-making in subsequent trials.
key_findings: Verbal feedback in natural language provides rich nuance compared to scalar reward signals.
Self-reflective error logs dramatically reduce repetitive failure modes in multi-step coding.
Outperforms traditional ReAct on HumanEval and decision-making benchmarks without fine-tuning.
significance: Direct foundation for the Starlight Santa Loop and weekly reflection recalibration logs.

label: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
description: Yao et al. (2022) established the interleaved Thought-Action-Observation loop that forms the standard foundation of modern agentic execution.
abstract: We explore the use of LLMs to generate both reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner, allowing for greater synergy between the two: reasoning traces help the model induce, track, and update action plans as well as handle exceptions, while actions allow it to interface with and gather additional information from external sources.
key_findings: Interleaving reasoning ('Thought') with environmental interaction ('Action' and 'Observation') prevents error compounding.
Grounds agent reasoning in dynamic environmental feedback.
Provides human-interpretable decision trajectories.
significance: Underlying paradigm for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, and all Starlight agent harnesses.

label: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls
description: Khattab et al. (2023) formulated programmatic optimization of LM pipelines using parameterized modules, teleprompters, and automatic metric compilation.
abstract: We present DSPy, a framework for programming with foundation models that separates the flow of your program (modules) from the parameters (prompts and weights) of each step. DSPy synthesizes and optimizes prompts based on a pipeline specification and training examples.
key_findings: Shifts prompt engineering from brittle manual tweaking to declarative programmatic compilation.
Teleprompters optimize in-context demonstrations and instructions against rigorous metrics.
Enables systematic refactoring of complex multi-stage pipelines across changing models.
significance: Informs the Starlight Prompt Engine and prompt library ranking rubrics.

label: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
description: Wang et al. (2023) created the first lifelong learning agent that continuously explores, acquires executable skills, and stores them in an iterative skill library.
abstract: We introduce Voyager, the first LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent in Minecraft that continuously explores the world, acquires diverse skills, and makes novel discoveries without human intervention. Voyager consists of an automatic curriculum, a skill library of executable code, and an iterative prompting mechanism.
key_findings: Vector-indexed skill library stores verified executable programs that compound over time.
Self-driven curriculum maximizes curiosity and systematic coverage.
Iterative execution error feedback refines code until it passes verification.
significance: Directly inspires the Starlight Skill Engine (`starlight-agent-skills` & `claude-skills-library`).

label: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
description: Schick et al. (2023) demonstrated that language models can self-supervisedly learn when, which, and how to call external APIs (calculators, search, translation).
abstract: We introduce Toolformer, a model trained to decide which APIs to call, when to call them, what arguments to pass, and how to best incorporate the results into future token prediction. This is done in a self-supervised way, requiring only a handful of human demonstrations.
key_findings: API calls represented as inline text tokens allows standard language modeling loss.
Filtering synthetic calls by whether the tool output actually reduced language modeling perplexity.
Substantially improves zero-shot mathematical and factual accuracy.
significance: Underpins modern MCP function calling and tool invocation standards.

label: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
description: Packer et al. (2023) designed a hierarchical memory architecture managing virtual context paging between main context and external archival storage.
abstract: Large language models are constrained by finite context windows. We present MemGPT (Memory-GPT), a system that intelligently manages different memory tiers in LLMs to effectively provide extended context within the LLM's limited context window, drawing inspiration from hierarchical memory management in operating systems.
key_findings: Operating System analogy: Main Context = RAM, Archival Storage = Hard Drive.
Self-directed memory editing via function calls (`memory_insert`, `memory_replace`).
Event-driven queue enables recursive memory pagination.
significance: Influences the multi-tier memory design in `starlight-memory` and `second-brain-vault`.

label: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
description: DeepSeek-AI (2025) demonstrated that pure large-scale RL (GRPO) directly on base models incentivizes emergent long-chain reasoning, self-verification, and 'aha moments' without supervised fine-tuning.
abstract: We introduce our first-generation reasoning models, DeepSeek-R1-Zero and DeepSeek-R1. DeepSeek-R1-Zero, a model trained via large-scale reinforcement learning without supervised fine-tuning (SFT) as a preliminary step, demonstrates remarkable reasoning capabilities. Through RL, DeepSeek-R1-Zero naturally emerges with numerous powerful and intriguing reasoning behaviors.
key_findings: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) removes critic model overhead, scaling RL efficiently.
Emergence of long reasoning trajectories with dynamic self-correction and reflection without human SFT demonstrations.
Distillation of reasoning patterns into smaller dense architectures yields frontier-tier performance at drastic cost reduction.
significance: Transforms model routing strategy across Starlight estate, enabling high-reasoning free/low-cost tiers.

label: Constitutional AI: A Framework for Machine Learning with Principles
description: Bai et al. (2022) developed Constitutional AI (RLAIF), using an explicit set of principles and self-critique to train harmless and helpful AI without human feedback on harmful outputs.
abstract: We introduce Constitutional AI (CAI), a method for training a harmless AI assistant through self-improvement, without human feedback labels for harmfulness. The only human oversight is provided through a list of rules or principles, forming a constitution.
key_findings: Phase 1 (SL): Model generates self-critiques and revisions according to constitutional principles.
Phase 2 (RLAIF): Model evaluates output preferences using the constitution to train a preference model.
Enables transparency and precise steerability of agent ethical boundaries.
significance: Direct theoretical inspiration for Starlight system governance, Taste standards, and safety gates.

label: The Hallmarks of Aging
description: Lopez-Otin et al. (2013, updated 2023) defined the molecular and cellular hallmarks of aging, providing the foundational framework for longevity research.
abstract: Aging is characterized by a progressive loss of physiological integrity, leading to impaired function and increased vulnerability to death. We enumerate and describe the hallmarks of aging.

label: Sleep and Cognitive Performance Research
description: Matthew Walker's research program on sleep and cognitive performance, establishing the mechanisms by which sleep deprivation impairs memory consolidation, emotional regulation, and immune function.
abstract: Sleep plays a critical role in cognitive performance, memory consolidation, and health. This body of work establishes the mechanisms and consequences of sleep insufficiency.

label: Fundamentals of Astrodynamics (Bate, Mueller, White)
description: The foundational textbook for orbital mechanics: two-body problem, orbital elements, maneuvers, and introductory mission design.
abstract: A classic introduction to astrodynamics covering the two-body problem, orbital elements, orbital maneuvers, and preliminary orbit determination.

label: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
description: Yao et al. paradigm enabling language models to explore multiple reasoning paths, self-evaluate intermediate choices, and perform lookahead or backtracking when problem solving.
